items.title: Not every landlord should switch to Airbnb
items.hook: Before you put your rental on Airbnb, ask yourself these three questions.
items.coreIdea: An honest filter for property type, location, availability and appetite for short-term letting. Builds trust by explaining when a traditional let may be the better fit.
items.notes: Belief: Lougher & Co advises on suitability, not just selling management. CTA: DM "SUITABLE" for a property suitability checklist.

items.title: The Airbnb income number that can mislead landlords
items.hook: A higher nightly rate does not automatically mean more profit.
items.coreIdea: Explain that revenue must be weighed against occupancy, cleaning, utilities, maintenance, platform fees and management time.
items.notes: Belief: proper comparison is net outcome and effort, not a screenshot of nightly price. CTA: save this before comparing options.

items.title: Can a normal two-bed flat work on Airbnb?
items.hook: You do not need a penthouse for Airbnb to work, but you do need these things.
items.coreIdea: Walk through location demand, sleeping layout, building rules, local permissions and guest appeal.
items.notes: Belief: suitability is assessed systematically. CTA: comment "2 BED" for a checklist.

items.title: What actually happens when a guest locks themselves out at 11pm
items.hook: This is the part of Airbnb nobody mentions when they say, “I will manage it myself.”
items.coreIdea: Explain the operational response: guest communication, access procedures, escalation and protecting the review.
items.notes: Objection: self-management is easy. CTA: ask landlords which task they least want at night.

items.title: The “guests will trash my property” objection
items.hook: The biggest fear landlords have about Airbnb is usually damage. Here is how good operators reduce the risk.
items.coreIdea: Cover screening, house rules, deposits or platform protections where applicable, inspections, cleaning checks and fast issue handling.
items.notes: Belief: risk is managed by systems, not wishful thinking. CTA: DM "PROTECT" for a turnover checklist.

items.title: Why a full Airbnb calendar can still be underperforming
items.hook: A fully booked calendar can be a warning sign, not a win.
items.coreIdea: Explain pricing strategy, minimum stays, demand signals and why maximising occupancy is not identical to maximising returns.
items.notes: Belief: dynamic management matters after listing goes live. CTA: save for your next pricing review.

items.title: The hidden cost of managing Airbnb yourself
items.hook: Most landlords only count the money they might save by self-managing. They forget to price their own time.
items.coreIdea: List guest messages, cleaner coordination, pricing, maintenance, review management and emergency cover.
items.notes: Objection: management fees are just a cost. CTA: comment "TIME" for a self-management task list.

items.title: Traditional let or Airbnb: start with this, not the rent
items.hook: Do not choose between a traditional let and Airbnb based on rent alone.
items.coreIdea: Set out the decision factors: goals, availability, property fit, risk tolerance, building and local rules, and desired involvement.
items.notes: Belief: the best strategy is property and owner specific. CTA: DM "COMPARE" for the decision framework.

items.title: The first 48 hours after a guest checks out
items.hook: A great guest stay is won or lost before the next guest arrives.
items.coreIdea: Show the turnover process: inspections, cleaning standard, linen, supplies, maintenance spotting and listing-quality checks.
items.notes: Proof/process video. CTA: follow for behind-the-scenes management systems.

items.title: Why “just put it on Airbnb” is bad advice
items.hook: Uploading photos is the easy bit. Operating a short-term rental is the business.
items.coreIdea: Break down pricing, positioning, operations, compliance, guest experience and review compounding.
items.notes: Belief: management is a system, not merely a listing service. CTA: share with a landlord considering Airbnb.

items.title: Your Airbnb photos are not just decoration
items.hook: The difference between average and great Airbnb photography is not what most landlords think.
items.coreIdea: Explain expectation-setting, showing usable spaces, light, layout, amenities and matching the right guest to the property.
items.notes: Belief: better presentation reduces mismatch and supports pricing. CTA: comment "PHOTOS" for a pre-shoot checklist.

items.title: The question to ask before buying furniture for an Airbnb
items.hook: Before you buy one cushion for an Airbnb, decide who the guest is.
items.coreIdea: Show how guest type drives bed layout, workspace, parking, storage, amenities and furnishing decisions.
items.notes: Belief: design follows demand, not personal taste. CTA: save before furnishing a property.

items.title: Why reviews are an operating system, not a vanity metric
items.hook: A bad review is rarely just a bad review. It is a clue that a system failed.
items.coreIdea: Show how feedback identifies issues in check-in, cleanliness, communication, maintenance or expectation setting.
items.notes: Belief: strong operators use reviews to improve the system. CTA: follow for practical hosting insights.

items.title: What Lougher & Co actually manages for a landlord
items.hook: When a landlord says, “What does management actually include?”, this is what we mean.
items.coreIdea: Natural founder-led explanation of the journey from listing setup through pricing, guests, cleaning coordination, maintenance and reporting.
items.notes: Offer clarity. CTA: DM "MANAGE" for a service breakdown.

items.title: The seasonality mistake that catches landlords out
items.hook: The same Airbnb strategy does not work every month of the year.
items.coreIdea: Discuss planning for demand changes, local events, pricing, minimum stays and cash-flow expectations without predicting results.
items.notes: Objection: Airbnb income is always the same. CTA: save for annual planning.

items.title: Why local knowledge beats generic Airbnb advice
items.hook: A strategy that works in one city can be completely wrong two hours away.
items.coreIdea: Explain local demand drivers, property type, transport, events, local rules and guest profiles.
items.notes: Belief: management should be tailored, not templated. CTA: ask viewers to comment their area.

items.title: Three signs your rental may be leaving money on the table
items.hook: If your rental has these three signs, it may be worth reviewing the strategy.
items.coreIdea: Use questions about location demand, unused availability, underused rooms or amenities, and owner capacity to operate.
items.notes: Attention plus qualification. CTA: DM "REVIEW" to discuss suitability.

items.title: The Airbnb myth: more bookings always means more money
items.hook: More bookings can mean more work, more turnover and not necessarily a better result.
items.coreIdea: Explain that the target is the right mix of stay length, price, guest fit and operational load.
items.notes: Belief: optimise the whole model, not one headline metric. CTA: comment "BOOKINGS" for a planning template.

items.title: What I would check before turning this long-term let into Airbnb
items.hook: If this were my property, I would check these five things before changing strategy.
items.coreIdea: A founder walkthrough framework: permissions, demand, numbers, layout, operations and fallback plan.
items.notes: Authority through decision-making. CTA: save this for a property review.

items.title: The landlord freedom test
items.hook: If your Airbnb needs you to answer messages all day, you have not built freedom. You have built another job.
items.coreIdea: Tie the promise of management to systems, handovers, clear communication and accountability.
items.notes: Belief: landlords pay for implementation and operational certainty, not information. CTA: DM "FREEDOM" for a management conversation.
